title: Monthly household budget worksheet with example numbers
summary: A plain monthly budget laid out as a worksheet, with a generic example household filling in every line so the shape is obvious.

blocks.title: A month, on one page
blocks.body: A budget that fits in your head is the only kind that survives contact with a real month. This worksheet has three parts - what comes in, what must go out, what is left to steer - with an example household filled in so you can see the shape before writing your own numbers.

blocks.title: The example is made up
blocks.body: Every number below belongs to a generic two-person household invented for this worksheet. They are there to show what a filled line looks like, not to say what your lines should be.

blocks.heading: Part 3 - what is left to steer

items.label: Example total assigned - in minus out must equal zero
To savings before the month gets a vote

blocks.heading: Using it with your own numbers
items: Fill Part 1 with what actually landed last month, not what should have.
Fill Part 2 from statements, not memory - the must-pays are where guesses hide.
Whatever remains is Part 3, and it gets assigned on purpose: savings first, then the flexible lines.
If the total assigned overshoots the total in, cut from Part 3 only. Part 2 cuts are a bigger project than a monthly pass.
Next month, adjust one line. A budget you rewrite from scratch every month is a budget you will quit by March.

items.label: Did any must-pay line move?
items.detail: Rent, insurance, and utilities drift; catch the drift once a month.

items.label: Did savings leave first?
items.detail: If savings is whatever is left over, the answer is usually nothing.

items.label: Which flexible line surprised you?
items.detail: Name one. That is the line to watch next month.
